question: In paediatric advanced life support, defibrillation is indicated for both ventricular fibrillation and pulseless electrical activity (PEA), with an initial shock energy of 2–4 J/kg.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Defibrillation is NOT indicated for PEA. PEA is a non-shockable rhythm treated with CPR and adrenaline. Only VF and pulseless VT respond to defibrillation. The energy dose of 2–4 J/kg for the initial shock is correct for paediatrics.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is FALSE. Defibrillation is indicated ONLY for shockable rhythms: ventricular fibrillation (VF) and pulseless ventricular tachycardia (pVT). PEA and asystole are non-shockable; they are managed with high-quality CPR and adrenaline, NOT defibrillation. The initial shock energy is 2–4 J/kg.
